replacements.text: The agent running a review round chose each reviewer's effort and tools. The panel's configuration file now holds both for every reviewer slot. Every reviewer receives the change as a diff file. A run that dies follows a fixed recovery sequence. The panel does not yet check that a run actually used its pinned effort.
The gates ran with the system bash first on PATH. The Homebrew bash hangs one hook test.
Code reviewers last judged commit e399db1d. Four prose-only commits followed it.
Tests check that every reviewer slot has a pin.
contracts.json pins effort and tools for every reviewer slot. No reviewer gets a shell.

The earlier design routed the OpenRouter mid-tier model away from whole-document reads. That constraint had no run record behind it. The only recorded reads of that shape on that model had finished. A constraint stated without its variables cannot be scoped or falsified. The design no longer encodes it. A slot that names a model runs that model. The recovery sequence answers for a death when one happens. It records every attempt. During this pull request's own review, that model finished 20 whole-document reads in 20.

Letting the dispatcher pick a fallback model freely was rejected. Vendors reprice and retire models under a remembered pick. Nobody can audit an improvised rule afterwards. A shell grant restricted by a command prefix was rejected. Both `git diff` and `git log` accept `--output`, so a prefix pattern is not read-only.

contracts.json holds eight slots by provider, tier and read scope. It also holds the staffing recommender and the trend checkpoint. OpenRouter reads a whole document at low effort and a diff at high. Codex frontier slots run at high. Mid slots run at medium. No pin names a model, because the routing table does that. Every tool grant is the Codex read-only sandbox or a list drawn from Read, Grep and Glob. No reviewer gets a shell pattern, because `git diff --output=<path>` writes a file.

The emitter writes each diff file over that reviewer's scope for the round. A reviewer with no shell can still read the change. Reviewers sharing a revision pair share one computed diff. Each reviewer entry in the round record gains effort and tools copied from its pin. A slot with no pin refuses the round and writes nothing.

Each artifact class keeps exactly one OpenRouter reviewer. Four reviewers move to Codex. Declared tiers do not change.

The gate's claim command takes `--effort` and records it. A run that died may be claimed again only as the same model one effort step lower or as the other provider at the same tier and scope. Anything else is refused and costs no attempt. A reviewer gets three attempts. Once it is out of attempts, the round halts only when the last failure on every route it ran on was a run that died or a transport error. A reviewer that runs out of attempts any other way is left without a report. The round is incomplete. A revert restarts a round in flight, because its attempts ledger gained a field.

harvest.md states the sequence, the failover slot, the diff file and the claim form. Nine scenarios with expected answers check that a reader holding only those files reaches the right dispatch.

The criteria attack panel needs the same pins, as slice B of work item agents-config-9k9.408 (predictable reviewer settings, as an interim cost control). It is a different skill with its own configuration file.

The round record copies each pin. Tests check that too. This pull request's own first round ran every reviewer at its pin on two vendors, with no substitution. Both recovery failures were real bugs found in review, reproduced and fixed with a failing-then-passing test each. A stuck round also costs coverage, because it can look finished with one reviewer never having read the change.

The written doctrine could send whoever runs a round by hand down the wrong path. Nine written situations were answered by a model given only the doctrine files. All 27 answers, three runs each, matched the expected dispatch. A reviewer without a shell could miss the change if its diff file were missing or covered the wrong scope. Tests cover the diff file's content, an empty change and an unknown revision. A diff git cannot compute refuses the round before anything is dispatched.
A reader holding only the doctrine files reaches the pinned dispatch. The reader reaches the failover slot and each recovery step.
The recovery sequence is one step down, then the other provider, then halt. A claim outside it is refused at no cost.

The agent running a review round chose each reviewer's effort and tool access. It avoided one model for whole-document reads on a belief that no run record supported. Review cost and coverage were unpredictable.

The panel's configuration holds effort and tools for every reviewer slot. Each round's record copies them from that slot's pin. Every reviewer receives the change as a diff file. A run that dies mid-reasoning retries one effort step lower, then on the other provider, then halts the round. Models still come from the shared routing table.

make ci, doc-lint and content-lint exit 0 at 5bc9e856. 27 of 27 isolated doctrine reads matched the key. Code and prose review circuits both reached a clean sweep. The gate does not yet check whether a run used its pinned effort.
The restated design deletes the scope-keyed tier rule challenged by this finding. It deletes the rule's tests too. The tier rule on main stands unchanged.

Nothing changes in this pull request. The verdict schema lives in another skill and is outside this change. The notes on work item agents-config-9k9.408 (predictable reviewer settings, as an interim cost control) carry the missing halt reason for a follow-on item.

A mutant that dispatched every reviewer at its declared tier in a sweep had passed all 219 emitter tests. That mutant now fails this test for the prose, spec and typed-code sweeps. The branch passes it.

An isolation trial showed that the isolated reader sees no instruction file. A reader with default settings sees the global ones. The isolated readers gave the keyed answer in 27 of 27 reads. No unit test exercises a doctrine evaluation.

The failover slot in that example is the OpenRouter frontier slot for a whole-document read. contracts.json pins it at low effort. test_a6_every_lens_pin_has_its_stated_effort holds that value. No test runs an example command, so the example was read against the pin.

The comment on MAX_ATTEMPTS no longer argues for another model on the same vendor. It now says why each attempt declares its transport and its model. The same argument is gone from the docstring of check_route.

test_a17_a_transport_that_is_not_the_failover_seat_is_refused failed before the change because the gate authorised the claim. It passes after. A mutant that drops the same-transport guard from the lower-effort branch also fails it.
The gate attaches halt guidance only to an `attempts-exhausted` refusal. It raises an `off-ladder` refusal without it. No test exercises prose, so the sentences were checked against that code.

questions.question: The failure concerns a reviewer using effort or tools it cannot work with, but the evidence only says tests check that slots have pins. What evidence, if any, supports this failure claim?
